title: Erzurum & Palandöken: Seljuk Monuments & High-Altitude Skiing
seoTitle: Erzurum & Palandöken Guide: Skiing & Seljuk Heritage
metaDescription: Combine high-altitude skiing at Palandöken (15 minutes from ERZ airport) with Seljuk madrasas, authentic cağ kebabı, and the Eastern Express to Kars.
quickAnswer: Palandöken Ski Resort sits just 15 km (15 to 20 minutes) from Erzurum Airport (ERZ) and 5 km from downtown's Seljuk monuments. With skiable terrain between 2,200 m and 3,176 m, Erzurum pairs reliable dry-powder skiing from December to April with 13th-century stone madrasas, wood-fired cağ kebabı, and direct rail links to Kars.

body.text: Few winter cities let you step off a morning flight, ski a 12-kilometer vertical descent before lunch, and walk beneath 700-year-old Seljuk stonework by late afternoon. Because Erzurum sits at roughly 1,900 meters on the high Eastern Anatolian plateau, cold dry air keeps snow crisp without coastal slush. Planning your winter schedule with [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) ensures airport transfers, ski-pass timing, and onward Eastern Express tickets align cleanly.
How close is Palandöken Ski Resort to Erzurum Airport?

Palandöken Ski Resort (branded with neighboring Konaklı as Ejder 3200) sits only 15 km from Erzurum Airport (ERZ) and 5 km south of Erzurum city center—a 15-to-20-minute highway transfer with no winding mountain passes ([KÜRE Encyclopedia](https://kureansiklopedi.com/en/detay/erzurum-palandoken-ski-center-12469)).

That short transfer is Palandöken's biggest practical advantage over European alpine hubs or distant Turkish resorts. Direct flights from Istanbul take roughly 1 hour 45 minutes, allowing skiers to hit the slopes on arrival day ([Powderhounds](https://www.powderhounds.com/Europe/Turkey/Ejder-3200.aspx)). The ski area spans 2,200 m to 3,176 m in elevation, offering over 28 km of marked pistes, a 12 km continuous run, artificial snowmaking, and floodlit night skiing ([Snow-Forecast](https://www.snow-forecast.com/resorts/Mt-Palandoken)). For a broader look at snow resorts across the country, read our [winter travel guide to Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).
What Seljuk landmarks (Çifte Minareli Medrese, Yakutiye) stand in town?

Central Erzurum preserves an extraordinary cluster of medieval Anatolian stonework within a compact 1.5 km walking loop. The late 13th-century Çifte Minareli Medrese anchors the old quarter with twin fluted brick minarets and carved stone reliefs, while the 1310 Ilkhanid-era Yakutiye Medresesi showcases a monumental portal and enclosed courtyard ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/tr/erzurum/gor)).

Start on Cumhuriyet Caddesi at Yakutiye Medresesi, built under Ilkhanid patronage and housing Turkish-Islamic and ethnographic collections—a role historically linked with the [Erzurum Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=EAR02&DistId=MRK). Walk ten minutes east to Erzurum Ulu Cami (Great Mosque), commissioned in 1179 by the Saltukid Emir Nasreddin Aslan Mehmet, and step immediately next door to Çifte Minareli Medrese (also known as Hatuniye Medresesi) ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/tr/erzurum/gor)). Five minutes further south stand the Üç Kümbetler (Three Tombs), conical-roofed stone mausoleums from the 12th to 14th centuries, and the 16th-century Rüstem Paşa Kervansarayı, where artisans still polish black Oltu stone (Oltu taşı) prayer beads.
Where do you try authentic cağ kebabı?

Authentic cağ kebabı—marinated lamb stacked horizontally on a thick iron spit and slow-roasted over seasoned oak or birch wood—is served in specialist kebab houses along Kongre Caddesi and near the Yakutiye district in central Erzurum. Order it by the skewer (şiş) rather than as a plated entrée so each slice arrives hot from the fire.

True cağ kebabı originates in Erzurum's Oltu district. The meat is seasoned simply with onion, black pepper, and salt, rested for up to 24 hours, and shaved onto metal skewers directly from the horizontal spit. Locals eat it wrapped in thin lavaş flatbread with charred green peppers, sumac-dusted onions, and strained yogurt, followed immediately by kadayıf dolması—crisp walnut-stuffed shredded pastry soaked in light syrup.
How does Erzurum pair with Kars and the Eastern Express?

Erzurum sits directly on the [TCDD Taşımacılık Eastern Express](https://cdn-api-prod-ytp.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/template/duraklar_ve_saatler.pdf) (Doğu Ekspresi) railway between Ankara and Kars, making a two-city winter itinerary straightforward. The rail segment from Erzurum to Kars takes roughly 4 hours through snow-covered gorges, while the highway drive via Sarıkamış covers 205 km in about 2.5 to 3 hours.

Travellers often spend two or three nights skiing Palandöken and touring Erzurum's Seljuk quarter, then board the regional or mainline train east to Kars for Ani's medieval ruins, Baltic-style basalt architecture, and frozen Lake Çıldır. Note that the seasonal Touristic Eastern Express (Turistik Doğu Ekspresi) sells sleeper compartments fast each autumn and includes multi-hour sightseeing stops (including Erzurum on the westbound run), whereas the daily mainline Doğu Ekspresi runs year-round with simpler couchette and seating cars ([TCDD Taşımacılık](https://cdn-api-prod-ytp.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/template/duraklar_ve_saatler.pdf)).

faq.q: When is the best snow at Palandöken Ski Resort?
faq.a: Mid-January through early March delivers the deepest natural base and coldest powder snow, though artificial snowmaking typically allows skiing from early December into April.

faq.q: Should I stay on the mountain at Palandöken or in downtown Erzurum?
faq.a: Stay at a ski-in/ski-out hotel on Palandöken if maximizing slope time is your priority. Stay in central Erzurum if you value walking to Seljuk landmarks and kebab houses—the resort is only a 10-minute taxi ride up the hill.

faq.q: Is Palandöken suitable for beginners as well as advanced skiers?
faq.a: Yes. Lower nursery slopes and wide blue runs suit beginners, while steep black runs off Ejder Peak (3,176 m) and off-piste bowls challenge advanced skiers.

faq.q: How cold does Erzurum get in January and February?
faq.a: Daytime highs in town often hover between -5°C and 0°C, with overnight lows dropping to -15°C or colder. Dry air makes the cold manageable with proper thermal layers.

faq.q: Can you visit Çifte Minareli Medrese and Yakutiye Medresesi in half a day?
faq.a: Yes. Both monuments, Erzurum Ulu Cami, Üç Kümbetler, and Rüstem Paşa Kervansarayı sit within easy walking distance and fit comfortably into a three-hour afternoon walk.

faq.q: Do I need to take the Eastern Express all the way from Ankara?
faq.a: No. Many travellers skip the 24-hour full rail journey by flying from Istanbul to Erzurum, skiing Palandöken, and taking only the scenic four-hour Erzurum–Kars train leg.
